sentences.text: Revenue compounded at 6.6% a year from $37.8 billion in FY2017 to $67.4 billion in FY2026 [F1][F10][F196].
The path was flat for five years, then two step changes: FY2023 revenue rose 17.7% and FY2026 rose 17.3% [D280][D421].
The FY2023 step came from the Cerner acquisition, which contributed $5.9 billion, or 11.8% of revenue [S61][D604][P48].
The FY2026 step came from cloud, where cloud infrastructure revenue grew 76.9% and added 13.7pp of the 17.3% total growth [D644][D645][D421][P17].
Cloud infrastructure is now the growth engine: 26.9% of FY2026 revenue, up from 12.9% in FY2024 [D639][D643].
Cloud applications added 2.8pp and software support only 0.5pp in FY2026, while software license subtracted 0.8pp [D668][D615][D682].
The filing attributes the cloud and software revenue increase to customers purchasing applications and infrastructure technologies and renewing cloud contracts [P17].
Operating income grew 16.6% against 17.3% revenue growth, so incremental margin was 29.4% and operating costs grew 17.7% [D422][D421][D442][D436].
Diluted EPS grew 34.3% against 36.5% net income growth as the diluted share count rose 1.7% [D425][D423][D438].
Operating margin was 30.6% in FY2026, below the 32.2% window median and well under the 37.6% FY2021 high [F34][D788][D787].
The largest move was FY2022, when operating margin fell 11.8pp to 25.7% as operating expenses grew 24.7% on 4.8% revenue growth [D246][F30][D249][D235].
That FY2022 drop was substantially due to litigation-related charges recorded to acquisition related and other expenses [P58].
In FY2026 the margin slipped 0.2pp: R&D fell to 15.3% of revenue and added 1.9pp, but other lines cost 2.1pp [D433][D399][D444][D445].
The offsetting cost was cloud and software expense, up $6.0 billion on higher infrastructure spending to support cloud growth [P19][P16].
Operating cash flow was $32.0 billion, 1.88x net income, above the 1.58x window median [F84][D408][D822].
The FY2026 increase was driven by higher net income and $4.6 billion of customer prepayments with a significant financing component [P6].
Free cash flow was negative $23.7 billion, a -35.2% margin, because capex of $55.7 billion reached 82.6% of revenue and 7.30x D&A [F104][D405][F94][D404][D410].
Investing outflows rose $30.1 billion mainly on a $34.4 billion increase in capital expenditures [P5].
Net debt reached $97.6 billion, or 145.0% of revenue, the 0th percentile against six software peers whose median net cash is -0.5% of revenue [D414][D415][D815][D816].
Total debt rose 39.9% to $129.5 billion on $42.7 billion of senior notes issued in FY2026 [D440][D413][P7].
Buybacks plus dividends were only $5.9 billion, 0.2x the negative free cash flow, and buybacks fell to $95 million [D416][F104][X155].
The balance sheet has flipped from a cash-return story to a debt-funded build-out, and $260 billion of additional data-center lease commitments sit off balance sheet [P1].
Cash and investments of $31.9 billion cover only 1.3 years of the latest $23.7 billion burn [D412][D419][D418].
Free cash flow has run below net income for two years, at -0.03x in FY2025 and -1.39x in FY2026 [D362][D409].
Net debt rose for a second year to $97.6 billion, and total debt grew 39.9% in FY2026 [D320][D367][D414][D440].
FY2026 net income in the table is proxy-sourced and differs from the 10-K figure by up to 0.60% [R5][F44][X20].
Free cash flow margin: a return above the 26.0% window median would reverse the FY2026 -35.2% trough, reported in the FY2027 10-K [D794][D792].
Capex: a figure below the FY2026 $55.7 billion would signal the build-out is peaking, disclosed in the FY2027 cash flow statement [F94].
Net debt: a move back above zero from the FY2026 net debt of $97.6 billion would confirm deleveraging, shown in the FY2027 balance sheet [D414].
